content:
Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that a former employee "for the benefit of OpenAI" stole trade secrets.

According to reports, as part of the lawsuit proceedings, Apple has directly contacted several former employees who are currently working at OpenAI.

According to a report by the Financial Times, Apple has issued evidence preservation letters to approximately 40 former employees.

A preservation letter is a formal written notice sent to an individual or organization, requesting that they preserve documents, records, and other evidence that may be related to a legal dispute. Such letters typically specify what needs to be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the alleged theft of trade secrets may involve more individuals than those named when the lawsuit was first filed last week.

A refresher: Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI and io Products as defendants, and also names former employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan.

You can read more details about Apple's lawsuit against OpenAI here:

  • Apple sues OpenAI, alleging former employee stole trade secrets
  • A single email mishap derailed pre-litigation negotiations between Apple and OpenAI
  • Apple's lawsuit filings reveal the number of former employees currently working at OpenAI
  • OpenAI says it has yet to see any evidence supporting Apple's allegations of trade secret theft
  • Following Apple's lawsuit, OpenAI's hardware launch timeline remains unchanged

You can read the full text of Apple's initial complaint here.
